summary: Institutional brokers need real-time cross-currency trade settlement with dual-authorization for large orders, margin validation, a 250ms latency target, circuit-breaker queuing, and ISO 20022 confirmation messaging.

criteria.name: Independent
criteria.rationale: The requirement relies on undefined external mechanisms it does not own or define, e.g. 'bilateral counterparty risk verification' and 'dual-authorization before routing', both of which imply separate, unstated authorization and risk-scoring services.
criteria.improvement: Either specify the dual-authorization and risk-verification mechanisms inline, or explicitly reference the separate requirement/system that defines them.

criteria.name: Negotiable
criteria.rationale: The text locks in specific implementation details rather than describing intent: 'Settlements must complete within 250ms' and 'Emits ISO 20022 compliant confirmation messages (pacs.008)' prescribe an exact protocol and exact latency figure instead of stating the desired outcome.
criteria.improvement: Reframe as a business goal (e.g. 'settlements must complete fast enough to meet regulatory same-day finality') and move the 250ms/pacs.008 specifics into a technical design or acceptance-criteria annex that can be renegotiated.

criteria.name: Valuable
criteria.rationale: A benefit is implied by 'execute real-time cross-currency trade settlements with bilateral counterparty risk verification' but no explicit business value (e.g. reduced settlement risk, regulatory compliance, client retention) is stated.
criteria.improvement: Add an explicit value statement, e.g. 'so that institutional clients can trade with reduced counterparty exposure and faster capital turnover.'

criteria.name: Estimable
criteria.rationale: Effort cannot be sized because the requirement bundles five distinct capabilities (authorization, margin validation, latency SLA, circuit-breaker handling, messaging) each with unresolved unknowns, e.g. 'Tier-2 thresholds' is referenced but never defined.
criteria.improvement: Split into separately estimable stories and define the Tier-2 threshold values and dual-authorization workflow before estimation.

criteria.name: Small
criteria.rationale: The requirement bundles at least five separable capabilities: dual-authorization for large orders, margin balance validation, a 250ms latency SLA, circuit-breaker queuing, and ISO 20022 confirmation messaging.
criteria.improvement: Decompose into individual requirements, e.g. one for dual-authorization, one for margin validation, one for circuit-breaker handling, and one for confirmation messaging.

criteria.name: Testable
criteria.rationale: Most bullets have observable, measurable outcomes ('Orders above $1,000,000 USD require dual-authorization', 'complete within 250ms', 'transition order to queued settlement state'), but 'bilateral counterparty risk verification' has no defined pass/fail check.
criteria.improvement: Define what constitutes a passing or failing counterparty risk verification (data checked, thresholds, and rejection behavior).

criteria.name: Acceptance Criteria
criteria.rationale: The bullet list functions as de facto acceptance criteria with concrete numbers ('$1,000,000 USD', '250ms', 'pacs.008'), but there is no explicit Given/When/Then framing and no criteria for failure paths, e.g. what happens when dual-authorization is not granted or margin is insufficient.
criteria.improvement: Add explicit pass/fail conditions for failure scenarios: insufficient margin, denied dual-authorization, and message delivery failure.

criteria.name: Unambiguous
criteria.rationale: Several terms are undefined or vague: 'bilateral counterparty risk verification' has no specified method, 'normal market conditions' in 'complete within 250ms under normal market conditions' is not quantified, and 'Tier-2 thresholds' is named but never defined.
criteria.improvement: Define 'normal market conditions' and 'Tier-2 thresholds' with concrete measurable values, and specify the exact checks performed during counterparty risk verification.

overall.verdict: This requirement bundles multiple undefined-threshold features into one story and is not ready for reliable test design until it is decomposed and its vague terms are quantified.

blocking_issues: The requirement bundles five distinct capabilities (dual-authorization, margin validation, latency SLA, circuit-breaker queuing, ISO 20022 messaging) into a single item, making isolated test design and pass/fail attribution unreliable.
'Tier-2 thresholds' is referenced as the trigger for circuit-breaker behavior but its numeric definition is never given, so tests cannot be constructed for this trigger.
'bilateral counterparty risk verification' has no defined method, data source, or pass/fail criteria, so tests cannot verify correct or incorrect behavior.
missing_information: Numeric definition of 'Tier-2 thresholds' for market volatility that triggers the circuit breaker.
Definition of 'normal market conditions' used to scope the 250ms settlement latency SLA (and expected behavior/SLA when conditions are not normal but below Tier-2).
The dual-authorization workflow: who the authorizers are, how authorization is captured, and timeout/expiry behavior if authorization is not granted.
The specific checks, data sources, and rejection behavior for 'bilateral counterparty risk verification'.
Error/failure behavior when margin balance is insufficient (rejection message, retry, partial fill).
Behavior for orders already in flight when a circuit-breaker transition to queued settlement occurs.
Recovery/retry behavior when the 250ms settlement SLA is missed.
List of supported currency pairs and any per-currency settlement rules.
Full ISO 20022 pacs.008 field mapping and any additional confirmation message types required for rejections/errors.
